a small origin story

I just wanted
to read a paper.

Then Zotero ate the RAM.

Not once. Not in some grand, cinematic explosion. Just the occasional, deeply annoying memory ballooning that turned a simple reading session into another thing to manage.

I wasn’t using every feature. I wanted to sort my papers, open a PDF, highlight a passage, and leave a note. A quiet little place to think.

So I went looking for something free, native to the Mac, and without the features I needed hidden behind a paywall. Zotero is already free and open source. I just wanted a different kind of reading experience.

Eventually, looking became building.

That’s chimpread: a small native Mac app for reading, annotating, and organizing papers. Free and open source, with no required account. Built around the idea that the paper should get your attention. The app should let you keep it.

— Ben
